newsitem.title: USA: Farmers to sell two units for $330 million.
newsitem.headline: Farmers to sell two units for $330 million.

text.p: Farmers Group Inc. said Friday it agreed to sell its Columbus, Ohio--based Ohio State Life and Investors Guaranty Life insurance companies to Great Southern Life Insurance Co. for a total of about $330 million.
Farmers is the U.S. insurance arm of British tobacco-to-financial-services group B.A.T Industries Plc, and Great Southern is a subsidiary of Kansas City, Mo.-based Americo Life Inc.
In London, B.A.T said the deal was worth a total of $330 million.

Farmers said the sales were in line with its plan to focus on growth in its Farmers New World Life Insurance Co., which markets its products and services directly rather than through independent organisations as these firms do.
Farmers Group, an insurance management and holding company based in Los Angeles, manages the nation's third-largest auto and home insurers and a major commercial lines insurer.
Farmers, based in Los Angeles, manages the third-largest auto and home insurers in the United States as well as a major commercial lines insurer.
After the acquisition, Americo will have about 1 million policies in force and more than $3.3 billion in assets under management.
